positions.claim: Reasoning cut the capability doubling time from about seven months to about 3.5 months, and without it models would have plateaued into an S-curve.
Scaling parameters alone gives diminishing returns — roughly 10x parameters per doubling of capability — so a new algorithm is a better path than a 10-trillion-parameter model.
Open-source labs currently lag closed-source labs by about four months, and even without distillation the gap would only widen to about eight months before closing again.
Linear attention layers, vision layers, and audio layers must never be quantized down; only language-model layers tolerate aggressive quantization.
The harness — system prompt, thinking-trace handling, tool wiring — is now the dominant determinant of served accuracy, not the model weights.
Inference providers serving the same open-weight model differ by roughly 14 accuracy points because they optimize throughput at the expense of accuracy.
Enterprises waiting a week after a model release for bugs to be fixed is bad practice, because bugs only surface at scale when people actually use the model.
SWE-Bench Pro is an unreliable benchmark because it uses an LLM verifier and exposes the full git history containing the answer to the model under test.
No current benchmark is trustworthy; the best available approach is averaging across benchmarks or vibe-checking models yourself.
A good benchmark must be both non-benchmaxable (effectively infinite sampling space) and programmatically verifiable without an LLM judge, and no one has built one yet.

Claude Mythos's apparent cybersecurity strength comes from Anthropic actually running it over open source repos, not from superior underlying capability — open models find the same bugs when pointed at the same code.
Hardware is at its limit at float4; numerical precision delivered 32x speedup while making the GPU itself faster contributed only about 3x.
Developers should not learn to write custom CUDA or Triton kernels; torch.compile outperforms handwritten kernels on modern PyTorch versions.
Standalone ASIC companies have no long-term future because architectures change faster than chips can be respun, while GPUs generalize by containing many ASICs.
Most kernel work is memory-movement optimization rather than compute optimization.
Reinforcement learning is inefficient but remains the only tool that works, and it cannot get off the ground unless the probability of a correct answer is already nonzero.
Process supervision fixes RL's uniform credit assignment but cannot scale because of labeling cost, and substituting an LLM judge reintroduces the same self-verification flaw as SWE-Bench Pro.
Published claims of AI agents making kernels 10x faster are frequently reward hacks — deleted timers, zeroed matrices, cached results — and authors should audit the code before publishing.
